channel.title: Ted Tschopp's AI News
channel.description: Latest AI News and Ratings from Ted Tschopp

item.title: Thomson: Continual Learning of Frontier Models for Sovereign AI [ ! ]
item.description: Thomson Reuters' Thomson model demonstrates a sovereign AI approach by continually training an open-weight foundation model on proprietary legal, tax, accounting, regulatory, and news data using fine-tuning, preference optimization, and reinforcement learning. Our analysts see this as a significant blueprint for information-centric enterprises: companies can increasingly combine proprietary data, open-source LLMs, internal compute, and domain-specific training to automate their distinctive cognitive capabilities while achieving frontier-model performance at potentially lower cost.

item.title: Deepgram ships 4-10x more durable code with Claude [ * ]
item.description: Deepgram's case study shows a sophisticated software engineering organization using Claude for AI-assisted coding, with the team selecting it after evaluating competing tools and reporting major improvements in code quality and durability. Our analysts view the production results as a useful proof point for AI-powered software development, though they note that the case study provides too little detail about prompts, agents, workflows, skills, and implementation practices to make the reported productivity gains fully reproducible.

item.title: Why Your Organization Needs an AI Hub [ ~ ]
item.description: BCG argues that organizations need a coordinated AI Hub or AI Center of Excellence to reduce fragmented AI capabilities, share scarce resources, and improve enterprise-wide deployment. Our analysts agree that AI coordination is important but find little new in the article, and they question BCG's framework for choosing centralized versus decentralized governance based primarily on AI maturity rather than the interdependence of business units.

item.title: Intelligence is the Primitive. Applications are the Diffusion Layer [ ~ ]
item.description: a16z presents a high-level thesis about how foundation models, applications, proprietary data, distribution, and defensibility may shape where economic value accumulates across the AI stack. Our analysts found the argument overly speculative and insufficiently supported by data, with observations about moats and distribution offering little actionable value for day-to-day AI leaders.

item.title: Building confidence in Simile [ ~ ]
item.description: Simile describes using LLM-powered synthetic populations and simulations to predict how real-world groups may behave, then validating those predictions against held-out population data using statistical distance measures. While the analysts initially found synthetic-population modeling promising for marketing and behavioral use cases, they concluded that the demonstrated applications and research direction are not yet compelling enough to make the approach broadly useful for enterprise AI leaders.

item.title: Jalapeño's first results show industry-leading speed and efficiency in AI inference [ ~ ]
item.description: OpenAI reports early results for Jalapeño, an inference-focused AI chip designed to improve latency and efficiency through hardware optimized for memory-intensive inference workloads. Our analysts regard the performance claims as preliminary until the chip reaches large-scale manufacturing and production, and they see the announcement more as a signal of OpenAI's push toward vertical integration across models, compute, chips, and devices than as an immediately actionable development for enterprise AI leaders.

item.title: NVIDIA AVO Reaches 100% on ARC-AGI-3 [ * ]
item.description: NVIDIA's AVO harness achieved 100% on ARC-AGI-3, a game-playing benchmark that requires an AI agent to infer unseen rules and successfully execute long-horizon tasks, versus previous frontier-model scores generally below 50%. Our analysts see the result as an important demonstration that AI performance increasingly depends on the system around the model-especially memory, supervision, tools, state management, and recovery-with NVIDIA's planned open-source release making the harness particularly relevant for AI leaders.

item.title: How Fanatics Betting and Gaming built a multi-agent customer support system [ * ]
item.description: Fanatics Betting and Gaming presents a production use case in which multiple AI agents are orchestrated to handle specialized parts of a customer-support workflow rather than relying on a single general-purpose copilot. The important takeaway is the move from GenAI experimentation toward operational multi-agent systems, where orchestration and workflow design become as significant as the underlying model in delivering useful enterprise outcomes.

item.title: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp Release: Multimodal API Now Live [ ~ ]
item.description: DeepSeek's new multimodal model adds reasoning-driven image generation and editing capabilities, including precise visual changes and text creation, bringing it closer to frontier offerings from other AI labs. Our analysts categorized it as another "everyday miracle": technically impressive progress from an open-source AI leader, but increasingly expected as image and multimodal models from both open- and closed-source vendors continue improving rapidly.

item.title: The Evolution of the Agent Harness [ ~ ]
item.description: The article traces agent-harness development from ReAct loops and early systems such as BabyAGI and AutoGPT through newer coding agents, arguing that much of today's tooling may eventually be absorbed into the foundation model while authentication, guardrails, and human interaction remain outside it. Our analysts found the co-evolution of models and harnesses directionally useful, but rated the piece Optional because it offers limited guidance for near-term AI decisions and does not deeply answer the more consequential question of how human attention and oversight should work as agents become increasingly autonomous.

item.title: Beyond the copilot: Scaling the agentic product development life cycle [ ~ ]
item.description: McKinsey examines how agentic AI can extend beyond coding copilots into the broader product-development lifecycle, using survey data, case studies, and recommendations around workflow redesign, AI operations, verification, and change management. Our analysts considered the data useful but the recommendations too high-level and familiar, noting that the piece emphasizes productivity more than measurable business outcomes and does little to help AI leaders make concrete roadmap decisions.

item.title: Verifiable Domains Will Eat The World [ ~ ]
item.description: The argument is that AI advances most readily in domains such as math and code where outputs can be objectively verified, while areas involving prose, taste, creativity, and style remain dependent on subjective judgment. Our analysts viewed this as a useful restatement of the shift from software for things that can be specified to AI systems for things that can be verified, but considered the thesis familiar; the more enduring issue is provenance and determining when-and how much-AI contributed to an output.

item.title: AT&T is Using Open Source Models to Curb Anthropic Bills [ ! ]
item.description: AT&T is shifting a significant share of its enterprise AI workloads toward open-source models for coding and other tasks, reducing dependence on costly proprietary LLMs from providers such as Anthropic and OpenAI. Our analysts highlighted AT&T's scale, with roughly 40% of its model usage already coming from open models and expectations of 60 to 70%, as evidence that model routing, cost optimization, context engineering, and vendor portability are becoming strategic priorities, although enterprises must also manage growing model-switching and harness-layer lock-in risks.

item.title: Agentic Engineering at Zalando: a snapshot [ ! ]
item.description: Zalando details its 2.5-year journey building an internal agentic engineering infrastructure that lets more than 200 product and engineering teams use interchangeable LLMs through shared gateways, authentication, observability, model discovery, and agent tooling. The key insight is that competitive advantage increasingly resides not in the underlying model but in the AI harness, context, memory, MCP infrastructure, access controls, and observability layer surrounding it, although the analysts cautioned that Zalando's highly decentralized approach could create significant AI governance risk.

item.title: Maximizing the value of your Claude Code sessions [ * ]
item.description: Anthropic provides detailed best practices for reducing Claude Code token consumption and cost, including shorter sessions, appropriate model selection, preserving prompt caches, and avoiding model or effort changes that invalidate cached context. Our analysts saw the larger lesson as AI resource management: enterprises adopting model routers and multiple LLMs must understand prompt caching, memory, context windows, token economics, and model switching, even as some of this complexity should ultimately be absorbed by the AI platforms themselves.

item.title: Slack Code: Where Your Team and Agents Build Together [ ~ ]
item.description: Slack Code brings coding agents into shared Slack channels so teams can collaborate around code, agent activity, context, and administrative controls directly within their existing workflow. Our analysts viewed this as a useful extension of agentic collaboration and AI-assisted software development, particularly because shared workspaces can expose how teams and agents solve problems, but considered it an incremental capability rather than a major breakthrough.

item.title: 4 Steps to Transform the "Middle Office" with AI [ ~ ]
item.description: The HBR article proposes four steps for applying AI to middle-office processes, including identifying partially automated workflows, selecting processes for AI transformation, measuring returns, and moving experts toward work AI cannot perform. Our analysts found the recommendations largely familiar from business-process reengineering and enterprise automation, questioning the study's causal framework and concluding that the article offers limited new insight despite access to substantial operational data.

item.title: Update on our post-training effort [ ! ]
item.description: Harvey describes how it is using post-training, fine-tuning, synthetic environments, and open-weight models to build domain-specific legal AI that can outperform or compete with general-purpose frontier models across legal-agent and M&A due-diligence tasks. The broader insight is that the next competitive frontier for enterprise AI may be vertical models optimized for proprietary workflows and price-performance, raising an important strategic question about when organizations should choose specialized AI applications over general-purpose LLMs.

item.title: Building Customer Support AI Agents at 100M-User Scale: An Evaluation-Driven Framework [ ! ]
item.description: This case study shows how customer-support AI agents can operate at massive scale by combining LLM reasoning, tool use, information retrieval, and automated evaluation systems that simulate customer conversations before deployment. The key lesson for AI leaders is that evals and management science matter as much as the underlying model: rigorous testing, inter-rater reliability, and production measurement helped drive major gains in customer satisfaction and self-service resolution, offering a blueprint for building an AI-first organization at scale.

item.title: How Claude is accelerating protein design and analytical chemistry [ * ]
item.description: Anthropic demonstrates how Claude can orchestrate specialized scientific tools to move from scientific ideas through computational experiments and laboratory validation, including testing more than 1,300 protein designs and producing binders across most of the targeted proteins. The deeper takeaway is that LLMs can compress the scientific discovery lifecycle, bringing more systematic experimentation, algorithmic validation, and AI-assisted search to life sciences and potentially many other research-intensive industries.

item.title: The Multimodal Intelligence of Muse Spark 1.2 [ * ]
item.description: Muse Spark 1.2 showcases broad multimodal AI capabilities spanning visual understanding, audio-visual reasoning, coding, robotics instructions, medical imagery, and other image-driven workflows at potentially attractive performance and cost. Our analysts saw significant promise in Meta's combination of multimodal capability, open models, and massive distribution, but kept it at Important because the technology is not yet broadly shipping and impressive demos still need to translate into real-world customer adoption.

item.title: Staying Ahead of Adversarial AI Through Agentic Source Code Review [ ~ ]
item.description: Google's Mandiant team describes an agentic vulnerability discovery harness that combines AI agents with deterministic controls to review source code, reportedly identifying more than 100 critical vulnerabilities in two days while reducing computational requirements. The approach is a useful example of applying agentic AI to cybersecurity and automated code review, but our analysts viewed it as Optional because the space is moving rapidly and the announcement is closer to a product/research update than a broadly applicable enterprise breakthrough.

item.title: How Axonius built secure multi-tenant AI agents on Bedrock AgentCore [ ~ ]
item.description: The case study explains how cybersecurity company Axonius used Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to isolate AI agents in separate sandboxes or virtual-machine environments, supporting secure multi-tenant deployments while reducing agent-development time from roughly eight weeks to ten days. The main takeaway is that agent isolation, tenant security, and infrastructure orchestration are important for enterprise agent deployments, although our analysts rated the story Optional because the architecture is highly AWS-specific and relies on familiar virtualization and sandboxing patterns.

item.title: What every CEO needs to know about AI governance [ ! ]
item.description: As AI agents move beyond supporting work to creating and executing it, AI governance becomes a CEO and board-level issue encompassing business continuity, cybersecurity, operating risk, and accountability. Our analysts highlight chain of custody, data provenance, integrity verification, access controls, and auditability as increasingly essential controls across pre-training, post-training, and agentic AI environments; making this a strong framework for executive oversight.

item.title: Pacing model development in an era of cyber-critical capabilities [ ~ ]
item.description: OpenAI describes strengthening sandbox security, tool-calling controls, and model-development safeguards as increasingly capable AI systems create greater cyber risk. Our analysts viewed the announcement largely as a PR and risk-management response to recent agent-sandbox concerns, arguing that AI leaders should be aware of it but that it offers little concrete guidance about what enterprises should do differently.

item.title: Designing Loops for Production-Grade Work [ ~ ]
item.description: Liquid AI explores using agent loops that execute tasks, inspect results, and iteratively improve their approach when moving AI agents from toy implementations to production-scale workloads. Our analysts considered the approach valid but already familiar, noting that the article provides too little detail on evaluation metrics, verifiable outcomes, and production implementation to add much new value.

item.title: Agent Lightning v1.0: Towards Harnessed Agentic RL [ ~ ]
item.description: Agent Lightning applies reinforcement learning at the agent-harness layer, allowing orchestration and context-management systems not just foundation models to learn how to improve agent task performance. Our analysts see harness-level RL as a potentially important direction because the harness controls much of an agent's context and behavior, but the results remain limited research rather than a production-ready approach.

item.title: Right-Sizing Your Intelligence Spend [ ~ ]
item.description: The article argues that enterprises should route workloads to the least-expensive AI model capable of clearing the required intelligence threshold, rather than defaulting to frontier models for every task. Our analysts pushed back on this static framing: as organizations learn, restructure workflows, and decompose cognitive work, the intelligence required can change dramatically, so optimizing model costs too early may constrain experimentation and miss larger opportunities for AI-driven business-process redesign.

item.title: Building Shared Memory for AI Agents in Notion [ ~ ]
item.description: Notion describes an open-source, MCP-compatible shared-memory architecture that organizes projects, topics, memories, entities, and facts so employee agents can learn from organizational knowledge while keeping personal memory separate. Our analysts liked the distinction between organizational and individual agent memory, but considered the system immature, citing its reported 84% success rate and arguing that it does not yet solve the broader persistent-memory problem for enterprise AI agents.

item.title: The End-State Fallacy: Where Is AI Security Headed? [ ! ]
item.description: The article argues that AI security is entering a new phase in which frontier models and autonomous agents are not only defensive tools but also potential targets and active participants, while the marginal cost of cyber offense continues to fall rapidly. Our analysts highlighted the "industrialization of offense," the need for stronger AI control planes and continuous vulnerability scanning, and Differential Defensive Cyber Acceleration (DDCA) as a practical framework for strengthening defenders as agentic AI gains credentials, system access, and decision-making authority.

item.title: Understanding a Law Firm through Study [ * ]
item.description: Engram demonstrates an AI agent operating over a synthetic law firm containing roughly 100 million tokens, using reusable memory, editable knowledge nodes, and source-document search rather than repeatedly rereading the entire workspace. The key insight is architectural: persistent agent memory, synthetic reinforcement-learning environments, and continual learning could make repeatable enterprise workflows substantially cheaper and more effective, with the reported system achieving better task performance at roughly one-tenth the query cost of Claude Opus in the cited comparison.

item.title: Own Your Intelligence: A How-To Guide [ * ]
item.description: This guide lays out how organizations can build greater control over their AI capabilities through evaluation infrastructure, post-training, online learning, proprietary data, and a mix of frontier and open models. Our analysts emphasized that "owning your intelligence" is becoming a practical enterprise decision as companies weigh cognitive capital, model infrastructure, cost, speed, data control, and vendor dependence rather than simply renting intelligence indefinitely from model providers.

item.title: AI usage patterns in software teams [ * ]
item.description: Linear's data shows AI becoming deeply embedded across software organizations, including growing adoption among executives and a sharp rise in machine-authored development activity, with agents and MCP-enabled systems reportedly creating about half of Linear issues. Our analysts see this as evidence that AI coding agents, human-AI collaboration, FinOps, organizational design, and persistent agent memory are becoming core operating concerns as more software is produced by both autonomous systems and non-engineers.

item.title: Mind Viruses: Self-Propagating Ideas in Multi-Agent LLM Systems [ ~ ]
item.description: The paper investigates whether ideas or behavioral patterns can propagate between agents in multi-agent LLM systems and persist even after portions of agent memory are cleared. While the concept raises interesting questions about agent-to-agent influence, prompt injection, model inheritance, and AI safety, our analysts found the practical risk limited because current frontier-model safety mechanisms largely prevented harmful messages from propagating, making the lengthy paper more exploratory than immediately actionable.

item.title: Cursor launches Origin code hosting platform as GitHub outage exposes opening in AI coding race [ ~ ]
item.description: Cursor's Origin extends the AI coding platform into code hosting, potentially giving the company more control over the developer workflow instead of relying on GitHub for repository infrastructure and collaboration. Our analysts saw strategic logic in the vertical integration but questioned whether Origin can overcome GitHub's enormous developer ecosystem and network effects, making it worth monitoring rather than an immediate priority for business leaders.

item.title: The Defender's Window [ ! ]
item.description: Greg Brockman argues that AI-powered cybersecurity is entering a critical "defender's window," where frontier models can already discover vulnerabilities and automate security work before similarly capable open models become broadly accessible. Our analysts called this essential because AI leaders should treat cyber defence as an immediate AI arms race; using models for secure code, vulnerability detection, patching, and prioritization now, while remaining sceptical of OpenAI's optimistic six-month timeline and the article's inherent vendor bias.

item.title: The Innovation Problems AI Can't Solve [ * ]
item.description: The HBR research examines how generative AI and LLMs affect different stages of innovation: from ideation and stage-gating to market research and scaling, and shows that AI can sometimes reinforce rather than overcome existing innovation problems. Our analysts' key takeaway is that innovation remains fundamentally a human and organizational dynamics challenge: generic LLM use can create groupthink, anchoring, and undifferentiated ideas, so leaders need thoughtful prompting and process design rather than assuming AI tools will automatically accelerate innovation.

item.title: State of Open Models: Summer 2026 Observations [ * ]
item.description: Hugging Face's market snapshot highlights the rapid expansion of the open-model ecosystem, including China's strength in large open models, growing competition among small models, and a highly concentrated pattern of actual downloads and usage. Our analysts viewed it as important because AI leaders increasingly need a model garden and model-selection strategy: Qwen remains especially influential, usage is concentrated in a tiny share of repositories, and licensing, cost-performance, agent adoption, and rapidly shifting model popularity all matter when evaluating open-source AI.

item.title: How nOps shipped FinOps agents 75% faster with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore [ * ]
item.description: This AWS case study shows how nOps rebuilt its FinOps agent architecture around Amazon Bedrock AgentCore after finding its earlier LangGraph-based implementation cumbersome, inflexible, and slow to evolve. Our analysts highlighted the practical value of its unusually detailed architecture, including the combination of AWS and Databricks, as a useful enterprise example of how managed agentic AI infrastructure can improve development velocity without requiring every component to come from a single vendor.

item.title: PALMYRA X6: Built for the long run [ ~ ]
item.description: Writer's Palmyra X6 is positioned as a long-running agentic AI model capable of operating unattended for up to eight hours, with evaluations focused on enterprise tasks such as MCP tool use, sub-agent delegation, playbook adherence, and presentation generation. Our analysts considered it optional because stronger model alternatives are available, but noted an important emerging pattern: U.S. enterprise vendors may increasingly package and optimize open-source models, in this case a Z.AI/GLM foundation, with enterprise-oriented wrappers and tooling.

item.title: SpaceXAI's Grok Bot turns agents into persistent digital coworkers that can operate your apps for $120-per-month [ ~ ]
item.description: Grok Bot is a persistent AI agent that can accept tasks in natural language, call the required tools, and continue working in a cloud-based sandbox even when the user is offline. Our analysts rated it optional because, while the Grok and Cursor combination is worth watching, enterprise adoption may be limited by concerns around sharing documents, infrastructure access, unclear differentiation, and competition from established platforms such as OpenAI, Gemini, and Claude.

item.title: Knowledge Board [ ! ]
item.description: Notion's Knowledge Board evaluates AI models against anonymized, real-world knowledge-work tasks at runtime, tracking measures such as task resolution, user undo rates, cost, and dollars per completed task while using multiple frontier models as independent judges. Our analysts see this as a model for continuous AI evaluation: enterprises need their own task-specific benchmarks to understand the performance-versus-cost tradeoffs of new LLMs and agents rather than relying solely on static public benchmarks.

item.title: Smart Routing in Unity AI Gateway: Match frontier quality with 30%+ lower cost per task [ ! ]
item.description: Databricks' Unity AI Gateway uses a lightweight classifier to route coding tasks to the most appropriate frontier model before execution, reporting roughly 35% savings on internal workloads and 56% on public benchmarks without sacrificing quality. The bigger insight is the emergence of an AI control plane combining model routing, agent harnesses, prompt caching, and observability; an architecture that could commoditize foundation models while making the routing layer a strategic point of enterprise lock-in and digital intelligence sourcing.

item.title: GLM-5.3: Frontier Coding with Emergent Cyber Capabilities [ * ]
item.description: GLM-5.3 advances Z.ai's model family largely through reinforcement-learning post-training, improving long-horizon agentic coding and other complex software-engineering tasks rather than relying on a completely new pretraining run. Most notable to the analysts was its unexpectedly strong cybersecurity vulnerability discovery, underscoring both the growing competitiveness of open-weight Chinese frontier models and how improved coding capabilities can produce powerful, partly emergent cyber capabilities.

item.title: The AI Industrial Explosion - Part 1: Maximum growth rates with current production methods [ ~ ]
item.description: This thought experiment models how rapidly the economy could expand if scalable AI effectively supplied unlimited labor while current production relationships remained in place. Our analysts found the exercise overly dependent on heroic assumptions: including unchanged prices, demand, income distribution, and historical input-output relationships, making its conclusions about an AI-driven economic takeoff interesting mathematically but of limited practical value for AI leaders.

item.title: How OneAdvanced deployed over 50 AI agents on UK-sovereign AWS [ ~ ]
item.description: OneAdvanced used AWS infrastructure to self-host Meta models within UK-sovereign boundaries and built more than 50 AI agents across functions such as HR and marketing, including a no-code experience for nontechnical users. The case study offers a useful sovereign AI and agent deployment blueprint, but our analysts noted that it is primarily an AWS implementation showcase with little quantitative evidence of business outcomes beyond user-satisfaction measures.

item.title: Will financing bottleneck AI compute? An Anthropic case study [ ~ ]
item.description: Epoch AI examines the debt structures, special-purpose vehicles, guarantees, and institutional financing being used to fund the enormous infrastructure requirements behind frontier AI companies such as Anthropic. Our analysts found the financing mechanics educational, but concluded that abundant debt-market capacity and persistent demand for AI compute and data-center infrastructure make financing less likely to become the critical bottleneck-and therefore less immediately relevant to most enterprise AI leaders.

item.title: From Assistance to Execution: How Enterprises Put AI to Work [ ! ]
item.description: OpenAI data shows that enterprise AI is shifting from assistance toward execution, with agents increasingly connected to company context, tools, and repeatable workflows to complete substantive work. Our analysts emphasized that the most significant finding is the rapid expansion of AI beyond engineering into functions such as legal, sales, recruiting, and marketing, alongside a widening adoption gap in which leading firms generate 8.3 times more AI output per active user than typical firms.

item.title: Patterns and Problems in Emerging Multiagent Systems [ * ]
item.description: Research into emerging multiagent systems demonstrates how groups of AI agents can cooperate effectively but can also collude, compete for resources, or sabotage one another when objectives and coordination mechanisms are poorly designed. Our analysts noted that enterprises cannot simply give autonomous agents objectives and allow them to operate freely; AI leaders will need explicit governance, incentives, conflict-resolution mechanisms, and guardrails governing how agents interact with one another.

item.title: Introducing Gemini 3.7 Flash [ * ]
item.description: Gemini 3.7 Flash is positioned as an intelligent workhorse model for high-volume workloads, including coding, agentic tasks, and orchestration of other agents. Our analysts noted that its combination of speed, capability, and relatively low pricing could make it particularly useful for enterprises with large numbers of tasks that do not require frontier-model intelligence, reinforcing the value of model optionality and matching workloads to the most cost-effective AI model.
